faq.q: What is the weather like in Marbella in July 2029?
faq.a: July in Marbella is hot, dry, and sunny. Expect daytime highs around 32°C, with sea breezes keeping it comfortable on the water. Sea temperatures reach 24°C, perfect for swimming. Rain is almost unheard of, with less than 2mm total for the month.

faq.q: Is July a good time for a yacht charter in Marbella?
faq.a: Absolutely. July offers the best combination of stable weather, warm seas, and long daylight hours. Calm conditions with 0.3-0.6m swells make for smooth cruising. It's the peak of the season, so book early to secure your preferred boat.

faq.q: What should I wear for a July yacht charter in Marbella?

faq.q: Can we swim and do water sports in July?

faq.q: What are the best destinations for a July charter from Puerto Banús?

faq.q: Do I need to worry about wind or rough seas in July?
faq.a: July generally brings light easterly winds of 10-15 knots and swell heights under 0.6m. Rough seas are rare. However, always check the forecast before departure. Your licensed skipper will monitor conditions and adjust plans if needed.

data.body_html:
Planning a Marbella yacht charter for July 2029? You're in for near-perfect conditions. July is the peak of the Costa del Sol summer: blazing sunshine, warm seas, and barely a cloud in the sky. This guide covers everything you need to know about the weather, sea state, and how to make the most of your day on the water.

July 2029 Weather Overview for Marbella

July in Marbella is hot, dry, and reliably sunny. Average high temperatures hit 32°C (90°F), with lows around 22°C (72°F). Sea surface temperatures reach a balmy 24°C, perfect for swimming straight off the boat. Rainfall? Essentially zero – less than 2mm for the entire month. You'll enjoy around 11 hours of daily sunshine, with the sun rising around 07:15 and setting near 21:30. The UV index is extreme (9-10), so bring high-factor sunscreen, a hat, and sunglasses.

Sea Conditions and Wind in July

The Mediterranean off Marbella in July is typically calm. Prevailing winds come from the east at 10-15 knots, creating gentle chop rather than rough seas. Swell heights average just 0.3-0.6 metres, making for smooth cruising on any of our boats. Whether you're aboard the compact Astondoa 40 or the spacious Mangusta 80, you'll enjoy a stable ride. The sea breeze actually provides a natural air conditioning effect, keeping deck temperatures pleasant even at midday.

Best Boats for July Charters

With calm seas and warm weather, every boat in our fleet is suitable. For smaller groups, the Azimut 39 (11 pax, €749/2h) or Astondoa 40 (9 pax) offer great value. For a premium experience, the Mangusta 80 (12 pax, from €4,719/4h) includes a free jet ski – ideal for July water sports. Larger parties can opt for the Ferretti 94 or Canados 86 (both 12 pax, pricing on request). All charters depart from Puerto Banús, Marbella's glamorous marina.

What to Expect on Your July Charter

Your day starts with a welcome aboard in Puerto Banús. Your licensed skipper will brief you on the itinerary, then you'll cruise the coast towards Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés. The water is crystal clear – perfect for snorkelling. Lunch can be at a beach club (book ahead) or on board with the included snacks and drinks. Afternoon swimming and sunbathing are a must. You'll return to port around sunset, with the golden light over La Concha mountain making for memorable photos.

Pricing and Booking Tips for July 2029

July is peak season, so early booking is essential. Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39) are €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for 8 hours – all inclusive. The Mangusta 80 starts at €4,719 for 4 hours, with a free jet ski. For other boats, contact us on WhatsApp for custom pricing. We recommend booking 4-8 weeks ahead. All prices include skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, insurance, and 21% VAT – no surprises.

What to Pack for a July Yacht Charter

  • Swimwear and a towel
  • Light cotton or linen clothing
  • Hat, sunglasses, and high-SPF sunscreen (SPF 50+)
  • Light jacket or sweater for evening (22°C)
  • Non-slip deck shoes or sandals
  • Camera or phone for photos
  • Your own snorkel gear if you prefer (we provide masks)

Alternative Months: June vs. July vs. August

June is slightly cooler (28°C) and less crowded, but sea temps are lower (21°C). July hits the sweet spot with warm seas and long days. August is equally hot but busier and more expensive. If you prefer quieter anchorages, early July is best. For guaranteed heat and vibrant nightlife, late July delivers. Check our Marbella yacht charter page for year-round options.

Frequently asked questions

July in Marbella is hot, dry, and sunny. Expect daytime highs around 32°C, with sea breezes keeping it comfortable on the water. Sea temperatures reach 24°C, perfect for swimming. Rain is almost unheard of, with less than 2mm total for the month.

Absolutely. July offers the best combination of stable weather, warm seas, and long daylight hours. Calm conditions with 0.3-0.6m swells make for smooth cruising. It's the peak of the season, so book early to secure your preferred boat.

Light, breathable clothing like linen or cotton, plus swimwear. Bring a hat, sunglasses, and high-SPF sunscreen (UV index is extreme). Evenings can cool to 22°C, so a light jacket or sweater is advisable. Non-slip deck shoes are recommended.

Can we swim and do water sports in July?

Yes. Sea temperatures of 24°C are ideal for swimming, snorkelling, and paddleboarding. Many charters include water toys or jet skis. The Mangusta 80, for example, comes with a free jet ski on 4-hour bookings.

Popular spots include Cala del Faro, Cala Cortés, and the coastline towards Estepona. For a longer trip, head to Sotogrande. The calm July seas make these routes comfortable and scenic. Your skipper will tailor the itinerary to your preferences.
